title: Lapita potters stamp geometric designs in clay
summary: Potters of the Lapita tradition impressed toothed stamps into clay to build geometric designs across vessels found in the western Pacific.

claims.text: Potters of the Lapita tradition impressed toothed stamps into clay to build geometric designs across vessels found in the western Pacific.
The Met’s 2002 overview uses about 1500–500 BCE. This broad material-culture framing is not a calibrated chronology for every island.
The style takes its name from a New Caledonian site. Its patterns sometimes include faces; pottery distributions should not be treated as a complete map of migration.

unresolvedIssues: Broad dating derives from a 2002 overview; island-by-island archaeological chronology is not independently checked.
review.corroboration: Te Papa’s thesaurus-based entry corroborates the technique and name, but supplies no independent chronology. The older Met date envelope requires specialist regional review.
